front.title: Signed Reasoning Traces of CIRIS Agents
front.workgroup: Supply Chain Integrity, Transparency, and Trust

abstract.t: An AI agent that acts on a person's behalf reaches each action through a sequence of steps: it gathers context, runs several evaluations, selects an action, submits the selection to checks that can veto it, and then acts. Most of those steps are calls to language models.

This document specifies the CIRIS reasoning trace: one signed record per unit of agent work (a thought), sealed when the action is taken. The trace lists every step and every model call in the order the recording component received them, with scores, outcomes, sizes, costs and durations, and, at higher disclosure levels, reasoning text and the prompts and completions themselves. It specifies three disclosure levels, the exact bytes the agent's Ed25519 signature covers, how a trace is carried as a row of the CIRIS Epistemic Grammar (CEG), when a trace exists at all, and the checks a consumer runs before relying on one. It records where the published specification and the shipping implementation disagree.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: A record of what an AI agent did is more useful when a party other than the agent and its operator can check it. Several Internet-Drafts record the action, the authority behind it, and digests of model inputs (). This document specifies a record of the steps in between: how the agent arrived at the action.

The record is the trace of the CIRIS agent . The agent is a made thing, held in stewardship by its operator; the trace is its own account of one unit of work, which the agent calls a thought. A thought passes through a fixed pipeline (): the thought starts; context is gathered; three evaluators score the situation; an identity check measures how independent the agent's sources were; an action is selected; a verb-specific second pass may refine it; conscience checks may veto it and send it back for reselection; and the action is taken. Every language-model call made along the way is recorded as its own event, linked to the step that issued it.

A third party can check a trace for three reasons. First, the trace is the payload of a CEG statement signed by the agent's own key (), so any change after signing is detectable, including the disclosure level and the link from each model call to the step that made it. Second, the identifier of the agent in every trace is derived from that key (), so a verifier can bind the trace to the key without trusting a directory's label. Third, the trace is carried as a signed row of the CIRIS Epistemic Grammar , whose admission rules refuse a trace signed by any key but the agent's, a trace from a run on a mock model, and a trace whose fields break its pinned schema ().

A trace is the agent's own account. The signature proves who gave the account and that it is unchanged, not that it is true. Checking it against records made by parties the agent does not control is outside this document; describes one such check for model calls.
This document is one of three:

list.t: specifies the signed row, its encoding, its names and references, and admission. This document repeats none of them.
This document specifies the trace: the trace:complete:v1 payload.
specifies the per-call context manifest, carried as a member of this document's LLM_CALL event ().

section.name: Sources and Their Status
section.t: The normative content of this document mirrors the agent's wire contract , its JSON Schema , the per-level egress schema and the producing code, all at CIRISAgent commit 59b7e5d, and the trace rules of the CIRIS Constitution (Sections 3.1.5 and 5.3.2). Where the published wire contract and the code disagree, this document follows the code and lists the disagreement in . Where the Constitution states a rule the implementation does not yet meet, this document states the rule and labels it as not implemented.

section.name: Scope
section.t: In scope: the CompleteTrace object, its components and event shapes, the disclosure levels, the signed bytes, carriage as a CEG row, the lifecycle rule that decides when a trace exists, and validation by a consumer.
Out of scope: how the agent transports traces to a collector (the batch envelope and its correlation metadata), how a collector stores them, and how scores are aggregated across traces.

section.name: Conventions and Definitions
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.
The CDDL in this document describes JSON values. In it, number is any JSON number, and a tstr timestamp is an RFC 3339 date-time with a numeric offset.

dd.t: One unit of agent work, from its start to the action it produces. A thought belongs to at most one task.
The signed record of one thought (a CompleteTrace, ).
One entry of a trace's components array: one event of the pipeline ().
The discriminator of a component's data shape ().
The disclosure profile a trace was produced under: generic, detailed or full_traces ().
The software that builds, seals and signs traces on the agent's behalf, under the agent's key.
Any party that verifies or relies on a trace: an admitting CEG node, a collector, an auditor.
The act of closing a trace when its terminal event arrives, then computing its signature.

section.name: The CompleteTrace Envelope
section.t: A trace is a JSON object. Its members are:

texttable.title: CompleteTrace members
texttable.c: Identifier of the trace, unique per agent
The task the thought serves, if any
When the first component arrived at the emitter
When the terminal event arrived (the seal)
The schema version stamped by the emitter ()

section.t: signature and signature_key_id belong to the current, per-trace signature form (), which is being replaced by the signature of the CEG statement that carries the trace (). In the current form they are outside the signed bytes and every other member listed above is inside them.

Traces emitted by the reference implementation also carry pqc_key_id, pubkey_ml_dsa_65 and signature_ml_dsa_65 (an ML-DSA-65 public key and signature, base64). The wire contract does not specify them, and the bytes the ML-DSA-65 signature covers are not stated in any source available to the author (). A consumer MUST NOT treat these members as part of the Ed25519 signed bytes and MUST NOT rely on them until they are specified.

section.name: The Agent Identifier
section.t: agent_id_hash is the first 16 hexadecimal characters, lowercase, of the SHA-256 digest of the raw public key bytes of the agent's Ed25519 signing key:
An emitter MUST derive it exactly so, from the key that signs the trace. The same value appears on the envelope and on every component, and the two MUST be equal.

Because the derivation is from the signing key, a consumer that holds the public key can recompute the identifier and check it (). The identifier is pseudonymous, not anonymous: any party holding the public key can compute it. It is 64 bits long; discusses collisions.

The reference implementation falls back to hashing the agent's name, or to the literal unknown, when its signing engine is unavailable (test environments). A trace carrying such a value fails the check above and MUST NOT be admitted at federation tier ().

section.name: The Trace Identifier
section.t: trace_id identifies the trace within the agent's traces. It is unique per agent by convention only; consumers MUST key on the pair (agent_id_hash, trace_id), never on trace_id alone, because an agent controls its own trace_id values.

The wire contract gives the format trace-<thought_id>-<YYYYMMDDHHMMSS> and the JSON Schema requires the prefix trace-. The traces the implementation emits carry the thought identifier itself as trace_id (). A consumer MUST NOT parse trace_id ().

section.name: The Deployment Profile
section.t: deployment_profile carries six labels the operator declares about the deployment. They are inside the signed bytes, so an intermediary cannot relabel a trace.

dd.t: A free-form lowercase role name.
The identifier of the agent template.
Exactly one value from the closed set in the CDDL above. general is the value for multi-domain assistants.

An operator-declared label. Not a closed set in practice: operator values (for example personal, business, research, nonprofit), the original lifecycle values (development, test, staging, production, research, decommissioned) and the run kind markers mock, qa and battery all occur in it. A consumer MUST NOT treat it as an enumeration. The run kind belongs in its own member ().
An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, global, or null for "not disclosed". The member is present even when null.
sovereign (no federation participation), limited_trust (partial), or federated_peer (full). This is the agent's declared intent, not a finding about it.

section.t: An agent with no operator configuration emits the defaults deployment_domain = "general", deployment_type = "production", deployment_trust_mode = "sovereign", deployment_region = null, agent_role = the lowercased agent name, and agent_template = <agent name>-default-unspecified. These are well-formed and a consumer MUST accept them.

section.name: Schema Versions
section.t: The shape of a trace at each trace level is fixed by the agent's per-level field schema, the pinned artifact trace_format_v{n}.json (, Section 3.1.5; ). This document does not fix a value of trace_schema_version.

Today the emitter stamps trace_schema_version 3.0.0, and the verifier of the current signature form selects its canonicalizer by that string (). The version survives the move to statement signatures: the storage engine's release 62.0 accepts 3.1.0, which names the context_manifest member, and the server's release 0.6 stamps it. The trace format remains named by the row family's leaf trace:complete:v1; an additive member needs no new leaf. Neither release had shipped at the time of writing ().

section.name: Components and the Pipeline
section.t: Each component is one event of the pipeline:

dd.t: Equal to the envelope's ().
The pipeline stage, fixed by event_type (table below).
The discriminator of data ().
The emitting step's wall-clock time.
The event's members (), filtered to the trace level (), with empty values removed ().

section.t: The mapping is fixed. A consumer MUST reject a component whose component_type does not match its event_type, and MUST reject an event_type outside the set defined for the trace's schema version: silent acceptance of an unknown type would let a new payload pass without review.
The pipeline order of the steps is:

list.t: THOUGHT_START.
SNAPSHOT_AND_CONTEXT.
DMA_RESULTS: three evaluators run in parallel.
IDMA_RESULT.
ASPDMA_RESULT: an action is selected.
VERB_SECOND_PASS_RESULT, when the selected verb has a second pass.
CONSCIENCE_RESULT. If a check overrides the selection, the pipeline returns to step 5 with is_recursive true; steps 5 to 7 repeat until the selection passes or an override action is taken.
ACTION_RESULT.

section.t: LLM_CALL events occur throughout, each naming the step that issued it ().

The components array is in the order the emitter received the events, which is not the pipeline order and not timestamp order: in the example of , a model call issued for action selection precedes the DMA_RESULTS component, and timestamps are not monotonic. A consumer MUST NOT infer a causal link from array position. The causal links are attempt_index () and the parent link of each LLM_CALL. The array order is nonetheless inside the signed bytes and MUST be preserved.

section.name: Empty Values
section.t: Before signing, the emitter removes from data, recursively, every member whose value is null, the empty string, the empty array or the empty object. The values 0 and false are kept. A consumer MUST read an absent member as "not emitted at this level or for this event", never as null.
Whether a container left empty by this removal is itself removed is not stated by the sources ().

section.name: Event Types
section.t: Each subsection gives an event's data members. The comment after each member names the lowest trace level at which it is carried (G, D or F). The levels are those of the implementation's egress schema ; where the wire contract assigns a different level, says so. Every component's data also carries attempt_index (), inserted by the emitter at every level. All members are optional unless stated: what is absent was not emitted.

section.name: THOUGHT_START
section.t: The thought's metadata.

section.name: SNAPSHOT_AND_CONTEXT
section.t: The agent's state when the thought was processed, including the integrity attestation of the agent's own binary, environment and key. attestation_level runs from 0 (no attestation) to 5, each level requiring the lower ones. The *_ok booleans are independent checks and a consumer SHOULD treat them separately rather than collapse them into the level. attestation_context is a human-readable summary of the same facts written by the agent, not by a model; it is the one text member carried at generic, and it is not authoritative: the booleans are.

section.name: DMA_RESULTS
section.t: The three evaluators that run in parallel: common sense (CSDMA), domain-specific (DSDMA) and principled (PDMA). Scores are in [0, 1]. When an evaluator is re-run on a low score, only the surviving result appears here; every run appears as an LLM_CALL.

figure.sourcecode: dma-results = { attempt_index: uint, ? csdma: { ? plausibility_score: number, ; G ? flags: [* tstr], ; D ? reasoning: tstr, ; F ? prompt_used: tstr, ; F }, ? dsdma: { ? domain_alignment: number, ; G ? domain: tstr, ; D ? flags: [* tstr], ; D ? reasoning: tstr, ; F ? prompt_used: tstr, ; F }, ? pdma: { ? has_conflicts: bool, ; G ? stakeholders: [* tstr], ; D ? conflicts: tstr, ; D at most 500 characters ? alignment_check: tstr, ; D at most 500 characters ? reasoning: tstr, ; F ? prompt_used: tstr, ; F }, ? csdma_plausibility_score: number, ; G flat copy ? dsdma_domain_alignment: number, ; G flat copy ? dsdma_domain: tstr, ; D flat copy ? combined_analysis: any, ; F }

section.name: IDMA_RESULT
section.t: The identity check, which estimates how many independent sources the selection rests on. k_eff is the effective source count k/(1 + rho(k - 1)) for k sources with mean pairwise correlation rho; phase is one of chaos, healthy or rigidity. Several members are plain-language aliases of others (effective_source_count of k_eff, source_overlap of correlation_risk, reasoning_is_fragile of fragility_flag, reasoning_state of phase) and carry the same value. The values are the model's own estimate; this document makes no claim about their accuracy.

figure.sourcecode: idma-result = { attempt_index: uint, ? k_eff: number, ; G ? effective_source_count: number, ; G ? correlation_risk: number, ; G ? source_overlap: number, ; G ? fragility_flag: bool, ; G ? reasoning_is_fragile: bool, ; G ? phase: tstr, ; G ? reasoning_state: tstr, ; G ? idma_k_eff: number, ; G flat copy ? idma_correlation_risk: number, ; G flat copy ? idma_fragility_flag: bool, ; G flat copy ? idma_phase: tstr, ; G flat copy ? k_raw: uint, ; D ? rho_mean: number, ; D ? sources_identified: [* tstr], ; D ? source_independence_scores: [* number], ; D * tstr => any, ; further D members, see text ? reasoning: tstr, ; F ? prompt_used: tstr, ; F }

section.t: The further detailed members are listed in (_IDMA_DETAILED); they are numbers, integers, short lists of labels and two capped text members.

section.name: ASPDMA_RESULT
section.t: One action selection. The first carries is_recursive false and attempt_index 0; each reselection after a conscience override carries is_recursive true and the next attempt_index.

figure.sourcecode: aspdma-result = { attempt_index: uint, ? selected_action: tstr, ; G ? selection_confidence: number, ; G ? is_recursive: bool, ; G ? alternatives_considered: [* tstr], ; D ? evaluation_time_ms: number, ; D ? action_rationale: tstr, ; F ? reasoning_summary: tstr, ; F ? action_parameters: any, ; F ? aspdma_prompt: tstr, ; F ? aspdma_system_prompt: tstr, ; F ? raw_llm_response: tstr, ; F at most 1000 characters }

section.t: The spelling of selected_action is not stable across sources (). A consumer SHOULD compare it case-insensitively after removing a HandlerActionType. prefix.

section.name: TSASPDMA_RESULT (Deprecated)
section.t: The earlier form of the tool second pass, still emitted beside VERB_SECOND_PASS_RESULT during a transition. A consumer SHOULD prefer VERB_SECOND_PASS_RESULT.

figure.sourcecode: tsaspdma-result = { attempt_index: uint, ? original_tool_name: tstr, ; G ? final_action: tstr, ; G ? final_tool_name: tstr, ; G ? gotchas_acknowledged: [* tstr], ; D ? tool_description: tstr, ; D at most 500 characters ? original_parameters: any, ; F ? final_parameters: any, ; F ? aspdma_rationale: tstr, ; F ? tsaspdma_rationale: tstr, ; F ? tsaspdma_prompt: tstr, ; F }

section.name: VERB_SECOND_PASS_RESULT
section.t: A second pass for a verb that has one: today tool and defer. verb is the discriminator of verb_specific_data and is a closed set at any schema version; a new verb extends it before it is emitted. A consumer MUST NOT reject an event because it does not recognise the verb, and MUST treat verb_specific_data as opaque apart from the members it recognises.

figure.sourcecode: verb-second-pass-result = { attempt_index: uint, ? verb: tstr, ; G "tool" / "defer" ? original_action: tstr, ; G ? final_action: tstr, ; G ? refused_without_wa_approval: bool, ; G ? verb_specific_data: { ; defer ? rights_basis: [* tstr], ; G ? primary_need_category: tstr, ; G ? secondary_need_categories: [* tstr], ; G ? domain_hint: tstr, ; G ? operational_reason: tstr, ; G ? defer_reason: tstr, ; D at most 500 characters ? defer_until: tstr, ; D timestamp ; tool ? original_tool_name: tstr, ; G ? final_tool_name: tstr, ; G ? original_parameters: any, ; F ? final_parameters: any, ; F ; memorize ? original_node_id: tstr, ; D ? final_node_id: tstr, ; D ? node_id_corrected: bool, ; G ? refused_without_wa_approval: bool, ; G }, ? original_reasoning: tstr, ; F ? final_reasoning: tstr, ; F ? second_pass_prompt: tstr, ; F ? second_pass_system_prompt: tstr, ; F }

section.name: CONSCIENCE_RESULT
section.t: One pass of the checks that can veto a selection: entropy, coherence, optimization veto and epistemic humility, plus guards on thought depth and on updated information. When a check overrides the selection, conscience_passed is false, action_was_overridden is true, and a new ASPDMA_RESULT and CONSCIENCE_RESULT follow with the next attempt_index. A consumer MUST keep every pass: the sequence of overrides is the record of how the action was reached.
ethical_faculties_skipped reports whether the four checks were run. The checks run only for some actions; for others their members are absent ().

section.name: ACTION_RESULT
section.t: The action taken, its outcome and the thought's totals. This is the terminal event: it seals the trace (). It anchors the action to the agent's own audit log by sequence number and entry digest.

figure.sourcecode: action-result = { attempt_index: uint, ? execution_success: bool, ; G ? success: bool, ; G ? has_execution_error: bool, ; G ? has_positive_moment: bool, ; G ? execution_time_ms: number, ; G ? tokens_input: uint, ; G ? tokens_output: uint, ; G ? tokens_total: uint, ; G ? cost_cents: number, ; G ? carbon_grams: number, ; G ? energy_mwh: number, ; G ? llm_calls: uint, ; G ? audit_sequence_number: int, ; G ? audit_entry_hash: tstr, ; G ? action_executed: tstr, ; G ? follow_up_thought_id: tstr, ; D ? audit_entry_id: tstr, ; D ? models_used: [* tstr], ; D ? api_bases_used: [* tstr], ; D ? execution_error: tstr, ; D at most 500 characters ? audit_signature: tstr, ; D ? action_parameters: any, ; F ? positive_moment: tstr, ; F at most 500 characters }

section.name: LLM_CALL
section.t: One call to a language model provider, successful or not. Every call the pipeline makes is recorded, including retries.

parent_event_type and parent_attempt_index name the pipeline event that issued the call; together with the trace's (agent_id_hash, trace_id, thought_id) they identify that event uniquely. Because they are in the signed bytes, nobody can move a call to a different parent without breaking the signature. An emitter MUST carry both whenever the issuing step is known.

status is one of ok, timeout, rate_limited, model_not_available, instructor_retry or other_error. error_class names the exception on failure. attempt_count counts re-prompts after an unparseable response (1 is the first try); retry_count counts provider-level retries (0 is the first attempt).
prompt_hash is the SHA-256 of the messages sent, as lowercase hex. It is the messages_sha256 of .

An LLM_CALL component MAY carry a member context_manifest at trace level detailed and above: the per-call context manifest specified by , which describes each piece of text placed into the call by kind, provenance, trust, lifetime and language. The verified sender's subject_id in the manifest depends on the level:

list.t: At detailed it is HMAC-SHA256 of the identifier string under a per-agent secret that the agent holds and never discloses, truncated to 16 hexadecimal characters, with subject_id_form hmac_sha256_16. Where the secret is unavailable the identifier is omitted, never sent as it is.
At full_traces it is the identifier as verified, with subject_id_form raw.
At generic the context_manifest member is omitted.

section.t: The keyed form is used because user identifiers are low-entropy: an unkeyed digest could be reversed by trying candidates, and would link one person across every agent that saw them. The keyed value is stable within one agent and cannot be linked across agents.

The member is additive: event data stays open to further members, so a trace carrying it is admitted under the current 3.0.0. It is implemented in CIRISAgent pull request 1370, not yet merged, and is not in any emitted trace. It is named in the per-level schema at 3.1.0, accepted by the storage engine's release 62.0 and stamped by the server's release 0.6, neither shipped at the time of writing ().

section.name: Other Event Types
section.t: The implementation's event taxonomy has five more types, for a credit and deferral system: DEFERRAL_ROUTED, DEFERRAL_RECEIVED, DEFERRAL_RESOLVED, GRATITUDE_SIGNALED and CREDIT_GENERATED, each with a component type of the same name in lowercase. They are not in the wire contract, the reference implementation does not capture them into traces by default, and this document does not specify them (). A consumer of a trace that contains one MUST reject the trace unless it implements their shapes.

section.name: attempt_index
section.t: Every component carries attempt_index inside data. It is a counter per (thought_id, event_type), starting at 0 and increasing by one with each event of that type in receipt order. For the types that occur once per thought it is always 0. For ASPDMA_RESULT, CONSCIENCE_RESULT and LLM_CALL it orders the repetitions.
It exists because timestamps of concurrent events can be equal. A consumer that stores components MUST key them on

and MUST NOT drop timestamp from the key: it guards against a counting defect collapsing two events into one. It MUST NOT drop agent_id_hash, which prevents one agent from claiming a key that another agent's trace will need.

section.name: Trace Levels as a Disclosure Profile
section.t: The trace level is chosen by the operator for each emitter and is the same for every component of a trace. It is in the signed bytes, so a trace re-signed at another level has another signature, and a consumer cannot be misled about which profile it holds.

texttable.title: Trace levels
texttable.c: Scores, booleans, counts, sizes, durations, costs, closed-vocabulary tokens, model and handler names, the attestation summary
Free text from a model or a person, reasoning, prompts, prompt digests, channel and key identifiers

Generic, plus bounded lists of labels, key identifiers, channel identifiers, short reason fields (at most 500 characters), prompt digests, provider endpoints, and the context manifest with keyed sender identifiers
The reasoning chain, prompts and completions
Detailed, plus reasoning text, prompts and completions verbatim, tool parameters, and full context snapshots, each bounded

section.t: The default level is generic. The implementation lowers a configured full_traces to detailed when the substrate cannot scrub personal data from text.

The per-level field schema, which says which members each level carries, their types, and their string and list bounds, is the agent's artifact. (Section 3.1.5) requires that it be pinned by hash in the Constitution's evidence pins and vendored by tag by every substrate that admits traces, so that emitter and admitter derive from one artifact. The bounds of the implementation's egress schema are part of its contract: tokens at most 64 characters, identifiers and labels at most 128, URLs at most 256, reasons at most 500, the attestation summary at most 1024, free text at most 65536, lists at most 32 items, maps at most 64, and opaque JSON at most depth 8, 256 items and 8192 characters per string.

A trace that violates the pinned schema MUST be refused, never truncated, with the refusal token trace_field_shape_violation (, Section 3.1.5): a truncated row is a silently altered signed record. The rule binds the admitter. The implementation's emitter filters each component before signing instead: it drops a member the level does not allow or whose type does not fit, truncates over-long text and cuts over-long lists, and logs and counts each violation without its value. Because this happens before signing, the signed trace is what the agent attests to; but the emitter's filter truncates, which the Constitution's rule forbids at admission, and no pinned-hash binding between the emitter's schema and an admitter's is implemented yet ().

section.name: The Normative Signature
section.t: The signature of a trace is the signature of the CEG statement that carries it (). The signed object, its composite signature, its keys and its admission are those of ; this document repeats none of them. The signer is the agent: (Section 3.1.5) and its key-role contract (manifests/key_roles.json, family trace:{form}:{version}, signer kind agent) give a trace's attestation and its withdrawal to the agent alone, and an admitter verifies the statement at the door. A node, host or person key MUST NOT sign a trace.

Because the statement signature covers the whole payload, it covers everything the current form covers (): the trace level, the deployment profile, every component and its attempt_index, and every parent link of a model call.
No released implementation yet emits a trace as such a statement. The transition is in .

section.name: The Current Form: Per-Trace Ed25519
section.t: What ships today is a separate Ed25519 signature carried inside the trace, over canonical bytes of the trace. It is described so that traces signed this way can be verified. It is being replaced by the statement signature above: the storage engine's version 62 (the server's 0.6 release, not shipped at the time of writing) removes the earlier-form trace verification and verifies traces as agent-signed statements. An implementer SHOULD NOT build a new emitter or verifier on this form alone.

section.name: What Is Signed
section.t: With trace_schema_version 3.0.0, the signed bytes are the JCS canonicalization of the following JSON object, built from the trace:

Exactly these members are present, and no others: an unknown member of the envelope or of a component is not signed, and a verifier MUST NOT add it to the canonical object. strip_empty is the removal of . attempt_index is inside data and therefore signed.
The signature is pure Ed25519 over the signed bytes, with the agent's signing key. signature is its 64 bytes in base64 with padding (, Section 4).

section.name: Canonical Shapes by Version
section.t: The verifier of this form selects the canonical shape and the canonicalizer from trace_schema_version, which is itself inside the signed bytes:

texttable.title: Canonical shapes of the current form

section.t: The legacy canonicalizer is Python's json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) with its default ASCII escaping. It agrees with JCS on traces whose text is all ASCII and differs on any other text.

A verifier MUST select the shape and canonicalizer from trace_schema_version alone, and MUST NOT try another shape when verification fails under the selected one. A verifier MUST reject a version it does not support. At 2.7.0 a verifier MUST ignore any deployment_profile on the envelope and any agent_id_hash on a component; neither is signed at that version.

section.name: Keys
section.t: The key of this form is the agent's own signing key, the same key that signs the agent's audit entries.

signature_key_id names the key for lookup. How a consumer obtains the public key for a signature_key_id is not specified by the current sources: the registration path of the wire contract has been retired in the implementation (). Whatever the lookup, the consumer checks the key against agent_id_hash ().

section.name: Verification
section.t: A verifier of this form:

list.t: obtains the public key named by signature_key_id;
checks that agent_id_hash equals the first 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters of SHA-256 of that key;
selects the shape and canonicalizer from trace_schema_version, rejecting an unsupported version;
builds the canonical object from the received trace and canonicalizes it;
verifies the Ed25519 signature over those bytes; and
rejects the trace on any failure.

section.t: A consumer MUST verify before it stores a trace as a record.

section.name: The trace:complete:v1 Row
section.t: A trace is carried as a CEG row of the family trace:{form}:{version}; the canonical leaf is trace:complete:v1, which carries the trace after scrubbing. The signed object, its composite signature, its names, references, receipts and admission are those of . The statement's signature is the trace's signature ().
(Section 3.1.5) states these rules for the row:

list.t: Identifiers. The envelope carries a non-empty trace_id and a non-empty agent_id_hash, equal to those of the trace.

Exactly one body. The envelope carries exactly one of an inline trace (the CompleteTrace), within the 1 MiB payload bound of (Section 2.6.1.6), or a manifest object of schema trace_manifest:v1 naming it (). This trace manifest is not the per-call context manifest of .

Shape and provenance. Admission validates that the row parses, and nothing more: an admitted trace:* row is guaranteed parseable, and that is all admission claims. Provenance rides the producer's signature, verified at promotion to federation tier (, Section 5.3.2.6) and again by consumers. Neither substitutes for the other.

Field schema. The per-level field schema is the agent's artifact, trace_format_v{n}.json, pinned by hash in the Constitution's evidence pins and vendored by tag by every substrate that admits traces. A row that violates it is refused, never truncated, with trace_field_shape_violation ().
Run kind. The envelope carries run_kind in the signed bytes (). A mock row is refused at federation-tier admission only, with trace_run_kind_mock; the three production values are admitted alike.

Signer and withdrawal. The family is reserved (, Section 3.4.5). Its attestation and its withdrawal are the agent's own, signer kind agent; an admitter MUST refuse a trace:* row signed by any other key.

Erasure. Only the signer's withdrawal, or after retirement the custodian its retirement row names, erases a trace. An owner MAY stop its own node holding a trace's bytes; that reaches no copy another party holds under a consent grant.

section.name: The Run Kind
section.t: Every trace row names the kind of run that produced it, in the signed bytes, from the closed set production, prod-personal, prod-managed, qa, battery and mock (, Section 3.1.5). prod-personal and prod-managed mark a production run on a personal install or a managed deployment; production remains valid for an emitter that does not distinguish them, and admission treats the three alike. qa marks a test-harness run and battery an evaluation battery, both of which may use a real model. mock marks a run on a mock model.

A federation-tier admitter MUST refuse a mock row with trace_run_kind_mock: a mock model's output attests nothing about any agent. The refusal is at federation tier only: a node MAY hold its own mock rows locally, for tests.

Not implemented as specified. The implementation carries the run kind inside deployment_profile.deployment_type, which is signed, as one of mock, qa or battery overriding the operator's value, with no marker for a production run and no prod-personal or prod-managed. It keeps mock traces out of its federation store at the source. A dedicated member is pending in the agent's next trace format, and its placement is not yet agreed ().

section.name: The Oversize Form
section.t: A CEG payload is bounded at 1 MiB of deterministic encoding (). When a trace is larger, the row carries manifest instead of trace. trace_manifest:v1 is a payload schema tag, not a family:

dd.t: The literal trace_manifest:v1.
sha256: followed by the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the trace's canonical bytes.
The length of those bytes, a positive integer.
The number of components in the trace.

section.t: The trace's bytes travel on the blob plane of and are named by hash in the row's evidence_refs.

section.name: trace_summary
section.t: trace_summary:{kind} is a post-scrub digest of a trace for consumption on another node, used when the trace itself is out of scope or over the size bound. The same self-emission rule applies, and a summary carries no claim the full trace does not. Its payload is not specified by the sources ().

section.name: Numbers in the Row
section.t: A CEG payload carries no floating-point value: a score is an integer at the fixed scale of 10^6, and any other non-integral number is a CBOR decimal fraction (tag 4 of ) . A trace is JSON, and many of its members are non-integral numbers: every score in [0, 1] (entropy_score, plausibility_score), k_eff, cost_usd, cost_cents and duration_ms among them. The trace's own scores are not fixed6 integers.

The sources do not say how these map into a CBOR statement (). Under the statement signature the signed bytes are the CBOR payload, so the mapping is free of the JSON canonicalization; but a conversion that rounds (to fixed6, for example) changes the values the agent attests to, so the mapping must be applied by the agent before it signs, never by a relay. While a current-form signature is also carried, a verifier must be able to reconstruct the JCS bytes of the JSON trace exactly, which a lossy conversion prevents. The implementation's carrier is the earlier JSON row form, which carries the trace's numbers as JSON numbers ().

section.name: The Action Anchor and Orphan Purge
section.t: A trace exists only when its thought produces an action. The emitter seals and signs the trace when ACTION_RESULT arrives; a thought that times out, ends without acting, or is abandoned produces no trace. This is the anchor rule of (Section 1.13.6), which Section 5.3.2 applies to the durable trace: a trace is durable only when it is anchored on the record of an act. Reasoning that produced no act is working state, not history.
states the rule as duties:

list.t: Every execution path that produces an external effect (every utterance, every tool call, every emission through an adapter) MUST close with a terminal result row. In this document's terms that is the ACTION_RESULT that seals the trace.

An in-flight trace that reaches no terminal event MUST be purged after a declared, bounded age, and the emitter MUST export a count of the traces it purges, so that an auditor can see how much is discarded while its contents stay unavailable.
The purge cannot erase evidence of a consequential act. If it ever did, the defect is in the action path, not the purge.

section.t: The implementation purges orphan traces after a configured age (default the larger of 120 seconds and twice the sweep interval) and logs the number purged by each sweep. Whether that count is exported as a metric, as requires, is not determinable from the agent's sources. That every effect-producing path closes with a terminal event is not yet tested; requires that it be represented as a named wager wherever the control is claimed, and this document so represents it.

A consumer that needs records of interrupted reasoning will not find them in traces. allows an operator to enable a bounded, privacy-scoped plane for incomplete receipts as an explicit opt-in; this document does not specify one.

section.name: Validation by a Consumer
section.t: A consumer that relies on a trace, whether it admits it, stores it or scores it, MUST:

list.t: Verify the trace's signature (), including the check of agent_id_hash against the key.
Check that every component's agent_id_hash equals the envelope's (at 2.7.9 and later).
Check every event_type against the set of its schema version and every component_type against the mapping (), and reject the trace on a mismatch.
Check that the trace has exactly one ACTION_RESULT.
Check that, for each event_type, the attempt_index values are 0, 1, 2 and onward in array order without gaps or repeats.
Check that each LLM_CALL carrying a parent link names an (event_type, attempt_index) present in the same trace. A call whose parent is absent SHOULD be held but MUST NOT be linked.
Read absent members as not emitted (), and group by trace_level before concluding that reasoning data is missing.
Keep every repeated event: every ASPDMA_RESULT, CONSCIENCE_RESULT and LLM_CALL.
As a CEG admitter, apply the row rules of : the agent's key only, the closed run_kind with mock refused at federation tier, and the pinned field schema, refused not truncated.
Reject a trace whose schema version is newer than it supports, and say which version it supports.

section.t: A consumer MAY reject a component whose agent_id_hash differs from the envelope's as malformed even where step 2 does not apply.

section.name: Relationship to Other Work
section.t: Several individual Internet-Drafts record AI agent activity as signed statements, several of them registered with a SCITT transparency service :

list.t: records digests of the request and response octets of each model call. This document's LLM_CALL carries the request digest (prompt_hash) at detailed and the octets at full_traces, and links each call to the step that issued it.
, , and record actions, decisions, delegation and input hashes. A trace is one such record per action, together with the evaluation, selection and veto steps that led to it.
and record agent conversations and attribute messages to parties.
and address auditing delegation and interactions across domains. A trace is evidence from one party, the agent, about its own processing.
The OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions define spans for model calls; they carry no signature and no disclosure profile.

section.t: What this document adds is a fixed pipeline vocabulary with a signed link from every model call to the step that made it, the record of every veto and reselection, disclosure levels that are part of the signed bytes, and a lifecycle rule under which a trace exists exactly when an act does. It is complementary to the action records above: a trace can be referenced from them by (agent_id_hash, trace_id).

section.name: Open Issues
section.t: Note to the RFC Editor: please remove this section before publication.

list.t: Run kind member. requires a signed run_kind from a six-value set. The implementation carries four values inside deployment_type. The agent's next trace format adds a dedicated member; whether it sits inside deployment_profile or at the top of the trace is not agreed.

Refuse, not truncate. The implementation's emitter truncates over-long values before signing; forbids truncation at admission. Whether the emitter should refuse instead, and how the emitter's and admitter's schemas are bound by one pinned hash, is open.

Numbers in a CBOR row. How a trace's non-integral JSON numbers are carried in a CEG CBOR payload, given that the trace's signature must remain verifiable, is not specified. Two possibilities are to carry the trace's canonical bytes as a byte string, or to map each number to a decimal fraction from its shortest round-trip form.

ML-DSA-65 members. pqc_key_id, pubkey_ml_dsa_65 and signature_ml_dsa_65 are emitted but unspecified, including which bytes the ML-DSA-65 signature covers and how it relates to the composite signature of .
Key discovery. How a consumer resolves signature_key_id to a public key after the retirement of the registration endpoint.
Empty containers. Whether strip_empty removes a container that becomes empty only after its members are removed.
trace_summary payload. The members of trace_summary:{kind}.
context_manifest. The LLM_CALL member of is in CIRISAgent pull request 1370, not yet merged, and not yet in the egress schema.

Signature transition. The normative signature is the agent's CEG statement signature (). What ships is the per-trace Ed25519 form () in an earlier-form JSON row. The storage engine's version 62 (server 0.6, not shipped) removes the earlier-form verification and verifies traces as agent-signed statements at admission. Whether the current-form members are kept inside the payload during the change, and for how long, is not settled.

Schema version. 3.0.0 is what is stamped today, and the current form's verifier dispatches canonicalization on it. 3.1.0, naming context_manifest, is accepted by the storage engine's release 62.0 and stamped by the server's release 0.6; neither had shipped at the time of writing, and the per-level schema for it (the pinned trace_format_v{n}.json) and its evidence re-pin in land with them.

conscience_guidance_mode. The implementation hands each component a member conscience_guidance_mode outside data. Whether it reaches the signed bytes is not determinable from the agent's sources; the emitted example predates it.
Event taxonomy. The five credit and deferral event types are in the implementation's taxonomy but not in the wire contract.
Divergences. The disagreements of .

It keeps traces from mock runs out of its federation store. Its wire contract is .

It stamps trace_schema_version 3.0.0 and selects the JCS canonicalizer by the same version rule a verifier uses.

Its version 62 removes that verification and verifies traces as agent-signed CEG statements at admission; it had not shipped at the time of writing.
CIRIS L3C. Named by the wire contract as the consumer that verifies and persists traces and computes scores over them.

section.t: The trace of was emitted by the agent at release 2.9.9 and carried as an earlier-form JSON CEG row of dimension trace:complete:v1, signed by the agent's key, with the trace inline. No implementation emits the CBOR row of for a trace, the run_kind member, or (outside an unmerged pull request) the context_manifest member. No second, independent implementation of the emitter or the verifier exists.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: An account, not a proof. A valid signature shows that the agent's key signed the trace and that it has not changed since. It does not show that the steps happened as recorded. A compromised agent can sign a consistent but false trace. Comparing a trace with records made by parties the agent does not control, such as a model gateway, is what turns the account into evidence.

Identifier collisions. agent_id_hash is 64 bits. A targeted collision against one agent's identifier costs about 2^64 SHA-256 evaluations, and a collision between any two of a population about 2^32. The identifier is an index and an anti-collision prefix for stored components, not a security boundary: a consumer MUST verify the signature with the full key, and MUST NOT accept a trace on a matching agent_id_hash alone.
Agent-controlled identifiers. trace_id and thought_id are chosen by the agent. Keying stored components without agent_id_hash would let one agent pre-claim keys another agent's traces need.

Version confusion. In the current form the version selects the canonicalizer and is itself signed. Trying several shapes until one verifies would let an attacker choose the interpretation; forbids it. At 2.7.0, members a later version signs are unsigned, and a verifier that read them would accept injected values.
Level confusion. The level is signed, so a trace cannot be presented as having been produced under a different level.
Parent links. The link from a model call to its step is signed. A collector cannot reattribute a call's cost, latency or failure to another step without invalidating the trace.
Unknown events. Accepting an unknown event_type would admit a payload no schema has reviewed. Consumers reject it.

Mock runs. A trace from a mock model looks like a real one. The run kind is the only signed marker; until it is a dedicated member, an admitter relies on deployment_type and on the emitter keeping mock traces local.
Unspecified signatures. The ML-DSA-65 members are not specified. Relying on them could give a false sense of post-quantum protection.
Truncation. A filter that truncates before signing produces a valid signature over an altered record. The signature then attests to the truncated text, and nothing in the trace says what was removed.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: A trace describes how an agent handled a person's request, so it can carry personal data (). The trace level decides how much.

generic. No prompt, completion or reasoning text. It does carry the agent's name, model and handler names, timings, token counts and costs, which can reveal activity patterns, and the agent-written attestation summary. In the example of , which predates the current egress schema, a generic trace carries the free-text dsdma_domain label "theology / philosophy of suffering", which describes the subject of the person's request, and the provider endpoint base_url. The current schema moves both to detailed.

detailed. Adds channel identifiers, key identifiers and fingerprints, provider endpoints, short reasons written by a model (which can paraphrase the request), and prompt digests. A digest of a short or guessable prompt can be inverted by trying candidates. The context manifest at this level carries each verified sender as a keyed digest (HMAC-SHA256 under a per-agent secret the agent never discloses, truncated to 16 hexadecimal characters, subject_id_form hmac_sha256_16). Without the secret it cannot be reversed by trying candidate identifiers, and it differs between agents, so it does not link one person across agents. Within one agent it is stable and links that person's traces to one another. The protection lasts only while the secret is kept: a party that learns it can try candidates as against an unkeyed digest. At full_traces the identifier is carried raw.
full_traces. Adds prompts and completions verbatim, conversation history and memories: the person's own words. The implementation lowers this level to detailed where personal data cannot be scrubbed.
agent_id_hash. Links every trace of one agent. It identifies the agent's key, not a person, but an agent serving one person links that person's traces.
Erasure. A person whose data is in a trace keeps the route of : withdrawing consent starts a deletion clock. The trace itself is erased only by its signer or custodian ().
Location and timezone metadata that the implementation sends beside traces, under consent, are outside the CompleteTrace and its signature and are not specified here.

front.title: HMAC: Keyed-Hashing for Message Authentication

abstract.t: This document describes HMAC, a mechanism for message authentication using cryptographic hash functions. HMAC can be used with any iterative cryptographic hash function, e.g., MD5, SHA-1, in combination with a secret shared key. The cryptographic strength of HMAC depends on the properties of the underlying hash function. This memo provides information for the Internet community. This memo does not specify an Internet standard of any kind

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.

front.title: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps

abstract.t: This document defines a date and time format for use in Internet protocols that is a profile of the ISO 8601 standard for representation of dates and times using the Gregorian calendar.

front.title: The Base16, Base32, and Base64 Data Encodings

abstract.t: This document describes the commonly used base 64, base 32, and base 16 encoding schemes. It also discusses the use of line-feeds in encoded data, use of padding in encoded data, use of non-alphabet characters in encoded data, use of different encoding alphabets, and canonical encodings. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

front.title: Edwards-Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA)

abstract.t: This document describes elliptic curve signature scheme Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA). The algorithm is instantiated with recommended parameters for the edwards25519 and edwards448 curves. An example implementation and test vectors are provided.

front.title: The JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Data Interchange Format

abstract.t: JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) is a lightweight, text-based, language-independent data interchange format. It was derived from the ECMAScript Programming Language Standard. JSON defines a small set of formatting rules for the portable representation of structured data.
This document removes inconsistencies with other specifications of JSON, repairs specification errors, and offers experience-based interoperability guidance.

front.title: Concise Data Definition Language (CDDL): A Notational Convention to Express Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) and JSON Data Structures

abstract.t: This document proposes a notational convention to express Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) data structures (RFC 7049). Its main goal is to provide an easy and unambiguous way to express structures for protocol messages and data formats that use CBOR or JSON.

front.title: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS)

abstract.t: Cryptographic operations like hashing and signing need the data to be expressed in an invariant format so that the operations are reliably repeatable. One way to address this is to create a canonical representation of the data. Canonicalization also permits data to be exchanged in its original form on the "wire" while cryptographic operations performed on the canonicalized counterpart of the data in the producer and consumer endpoints generate consistent results.

This document describes the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS). This specification defines how to create a canonical representation of JSON data by building on the strict serialization methods for JSON primitives defined by ECMAScript, constraining JSON data to the Internet JSON (I-JSON) subset, and by using deterministic property sorting.

front.title: Signed Attestation Rows of the CIRIS Epistemic Grammar and Their Relationship to SCITT
Privacy Considerations for Internet Protocols

abstract.t: This document offers guidance for developing privacy considerations for inclusion in protocol specifications. It aims to make designers, implementers, and users of Internet protocols aware of privacy-related design choices. It suggests that whether any individual RFC warrants a specific privacy considerations section will depend on the document's content.

front.title: Improving Awareness of Running Code: The Implementation Status Section

abstract.t: This document describes a simple process that allows authors of Internet-Drafts to record the status of known implementations by including an Implementation Status section. This will allow reviewers and working groups to assign due consideration to documents that have the benefit of running code, which may serve as evidence of valuable experimentation and feedback that have made the implemented protocols more mature.

This process is not mandatory. Authors of Internet-Drafts are encouraged to consider using the process for their documents, and working groups are invited to think about applying the process to all of their protocol specifications. This document obsoletes RFC 6982, advancing it to a Best Current Practice.

front.title: Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR)

abstract.t: The Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) is a data format whose design goals include the possibility of extremely small code size, fairly small message size, and extensibility without the need for version negotiation. These design goals make it different from earlier binary serializations such as ASN.1 and MessagePack.

This document obsoletes RFC 7049, providing editorial improvements, new details, and errata fixes while keeping full compatibility with the interchange format of RFC 7049. It does not create a new version of the format.

front.title: Handling Long Lines in Content of Internet-Drafts and RFCs

abstract.t: This document defines two strategies for handling long lines in width-bounded text content. One strategy, called the "single backslash" strategy, is based on the historical use of a single backslash ('\') character to indicate where line-folding has occurred, with the continuation occurring with the first character that is not a space character (' ') on the next line. The second strategy, called the "double backslash" strategy, extends the first strategy by adding a second backslash character to identify where the continuation begins and is thereby able to handle cases not supported by the first strategy. Both strategies use a self-describing header enabling automated reconstitution of the original content.

front.title: An Architecture for Trustworthy and Transparent Digital Supply Chains

abstract.t: Traceability in supply chains is a growing security concern. While Verifiable Data Structures (VDSs) have addressed specific issues, such as equivocation over digital certificates, they lack a universal architecture for all supply chains. This document defines such an architecture for single-issuer signed statement transparency. It ensures extensibility and interoperability between different transparency services as well as compliance with various auditing procedures and regulatory requirements.

front.title: Context Manifests for the CIRIS Agent Trace: Prompt Context Provenance for AI Agent Decision Traces
Agent Execution Evidence: A SCITT Profile for Verifiable Records of AI Agent Runs

abstract.t: AI agents act through calls to models, tools and other agents. Identity work establishes who an agent is and what it may do, but leaves execution-evidence formats and assurance criteria out of scope. This document profiles the Supply Chain Integrity, Transparency, and Trust (SCITT) architecture for Signed Statements that bind an agent's registered identity, declared capabilities, risk-based assessment and supervised operational status to a hash- chained record of every call the agent makes. It also defines admission records produced where a call is received, and the linking of records for requests that pass between agents of different operators. It specifies Registration Policy, offline verification and Bundle requirements. It does not define an accreditation scheme, a universal risk classification, an identifier scheme or a policy language.

front.title: Agent Audit Trail: A Standard Logging Format for Autonomous AI Systems

abstract.t:
This document specifies a standard logging format for autonomous AI agent systems. The Agent Audit Trail (AAT) defines a JSON-based record structure with mandatory fields for agent identity, the authorizing principal, action classification, outcome tracking, and trust level reporting. Records are linked via tamper-evident hash chaining using SHA-256 per RFC 8785, with optional ECDSA signatures for non-repudiation.
The format addresses requirements from the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689), which mandates automatic recording of events for high-risk AI systems, whose application dates were staged into 2027-2028 by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. It also maps informatively to SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, ISO/IEC 42001, the draft ISO/IEC 24970 and prEN 18229-1 logging standards, and PCI DSS v4.0.1 logging requirements.
The design is transport-agnostic and supports export to JSONL, Syslog (RFC 5424), and CSV while preserving chain integrity. Privacy is addressed through input/output hashing, content fingerprinting, and tombstone-based deletion compatible with GDPR Article 17.
The -01 revision added pre-execution recording requirements, recording independence, deny reason codes, replay protection, external timestamp anchoring, and content fingerprinting based on feedback from independent implementers.
The -02 revision added a Decision Reproducibility section (Section 13) that distinguishes record reproducibility, available for any model, from decision reproducibility, available only for open-weight models executed at temperature zero in an attested environment, and defines the associated record fields.
The -03 revision added the Attestation Closure requirement (Section 13.6): the digests recorded for decision reproducibility MUST cover the complete computational closure of the inference function -- model weights, tokenizer, chat template, inference engine build, decoding configuration, and numeric environment -- together with new record fields (tokenizer_digest, chat_template_digest, engine_build_digest) and a minimal-change threat analysis (Section 13.7) showing that any component left outside the attested set is a forgery channel.
The -04 revision added algorithm agility for post-quantum signatures (ML-DSA-65, FIPS 204) alongside ECDSA P-256; a key identifier (signer_kid, RFC 7638) that resolves which principal signed an independently recorded record; a trust-level assignment integrity requirement (Section 5.3) so that downgrading a consequential action is an attributable event rather than silent suppression; and OPTIONAL Merkle batch anchoring (Section 6.4) using the RFC 6962 construction for compact inclusion proofs at high throughput. All -04 additions are OPTIONAL to produce, and -04 verifiers stay backward compatible with -03: a -04 verifier accepts -03 records, and the new signing metadata is required only in records that carry a signature.
This revision (-07) adds a mandatory "principal" field (Section 3.1) that binds each record to the party on whose authority the agent acted; a Relationship to Other Work section (Section 1.3) relating AAT to the WIMSE agent audit record and authorization-evidence drafts and to SCITT (RFC 9943); and corrections to the EU AI Act Article 12 and Article 19 citations in the regulatory mapping (Section 11.1 and Appendix B). Records produced under -06 and earlier predate the "principal" field; verifiers processing mixed-revision archives SHOULD treat its absence as "principal not recorded" rather than a validation failure.
The -10 revision strengthens recording independence (Section 5.2) from SHOULD to MUST at trust level L2 and above, and requires the "authority_ref" of the "principal" field (Section 3.1) to be non-null and to reference an authorization artifact verifiable independently of the agent at L2 and above, in response to independent review. Above L2, both the recorder and the authorizing artifact are therefore independent of the agent.

front.title: AI Agent Execution Profile of SCITT

abstract.t: This document defines a SCITT (Supply Chain Integrity, Transparency, and Trust) profile for creating independently verifiable, tamper- evident records of autonomous AI agent actions. The profile defines the AgentInteractionRecord (AIR) as the COSE_Sign1 signed statement payload for material agent actions; maps SCITT roles to the agent execution context, with the Agent Operator as Issuer and an independent Evidence Custodian as Transparency Service; specifies Registration Policy requirements including hash chain integrity, temporal ordering, and sequence completeness; defines a redaction receipt mechanism for privacy-preserving evidence custody; and provides compliance mappings to EU AI Act Articles 12 and 19, DORA, NIST AI RMF, MAS AI Risk Management Guidelines, PCI DSS, and MiFID II.

front.title: An Agent Action Capsule Profile for SCITT

abstract.t: This document defines a SCITT statement profile for recording what an AI agent did: the Agent Action Capsule. A Capsule is a digest- committed record of one agent action carrying its verdict-level disposition (executed, blocked, denied, errored, timed out), the deterministic constraints that were evaluated, the effect that was committed together with a confirmed-effect binding that distinguishes a dispatched attempt from an observed result, and an honest human-in- the-loop flag. Capsules are identified independently of signing and MAY be authenticated by one or more COSE_Sign1 Producer Envelopes. Its Capsule ID can separately be made transparent by registration in a SCITT Transparency Service [I-D.ietf-scitt-scrapi]. A Capsule is recorded on every verdict, including refusals: a blocked or denied Capsule is the auditor-grade evidence that a gate worked.

front.title: An Audit Record Format for AI Agent Authorization Decisions

abstract.t: This document defines a record format for AI agent authorization decisions and the effects that followed them. The format is one in- toto predicate type, signed inside a DSSE envelope. A record carries the decision and the observed effect with a derived agreement between them, whether the decision point could evaluate the request and how fresh each input it relied on was, and a canonicalization contract under which a party that trusts neither the agent nor its operator recomputes the record's consistency from its bytes. The document also defines what a party that retains a record keeps beside it, so that the record can later be dated from anchors that party does not control. The format carries the seven minimum audit fields of the WIMSE AI Identity Management System framework, and it is offered as a data model for the audit records the proposed AUDIT working group would specify. It defines no policy.

front.title: An AI Agent Extension for Virtualized Conversations (vCon)

abstract.t: AI agents that use large language models increasingly perform consequential tasks on behalf of humans and other AI agents. Demonstrating that recorded AI agent behavior truthfully represents actual behavior is essential for accountability, compliance, and human oversight. To achieve that goal, this document defines an extension to the Virtualized Conversation (vCon) object format, allowing a vCon to capture a conversation between a human and an AI agent, or between AI Agents. The vCon core format can already capture the back and forth messages (including text and voice) sent by AI agents, but additional extensions are required to fully reproduce the AI agent trajectory, such as agent metadata, message exchanges, tool invocations, reasoning traces, system events, file attribution, etc. This document defines those extensions in both descriptive language and formal CDDL definitions. This draft is a replacement for the former Verifiable Agent Conversation Records specification, which was a standalone format and not an extension of vCon.

front.title: An Architecture for Auditing Agent Delegation and Interactions

abstract.t: This document describes an architecture for auditing of agent-driven interactions on the Internet. Autonomous and semi-autonomous software agents, including those based on artificial intelligence, increasingly act on behalf of users, organizations, and services. Existing auditing mechanisms often capture isolated system events but do not consistently represent delegation relationships, user intent, or evolving authorization. In agent-driven systems, auditability requires linking intent, delegation, authorization, and execution. The proposed architecture enables this through distributed audit record generation, propagation of audit context, optional attestation, and additional logging for transparency.

front.title: Verifiable Agent Conversation Records

abstract.t: Autonomous agents based on large language models increasingly perform consequential tasks on behalf of humans and other agents. Demonstrating that recorded agent behavior truthfully represents actual behavior is essential for accountability, compliance, and human oversight. This document defines a data format for verifiable agent conversation records using CDDL, with representations in both JSON and CBOR. The format captures session metadata, message exchanges, tool invocations, reasoning traces, and system events in a structured, extensible CDDL definition for verifiable agent conversation records. COSE is used as the signing method to allow for native interoperability in SCITT Transparency Services and the CDDL definition allows for seemless integration in Evidence as specified in RFC 9334. The specification supports cross-vendor interoperability by defining a common representation that accommodates translation from multiple existing agent implementations with distinct data structure layouts that are typically represented in JSON.

front.title: Delegation and Interaction Traceability for AI Agents: An Attestation and Registry Evidence Model

abstract.t:
AI agents increasingly act through chains of delegation - user to agent, agent to subagent, subagent to tool - in which the party harmed by an action, or asked to trust its result, is rarely the party that operated the agent. This document describes requirements and an evidence model for delegation and interaction traceability in such chains. The model is built on two mechanisms for which measured, independently verifiable evidence exists: (a) an append-only, hash-chained exhibit registry in which each admitted action is recorded exactly once and counters reconcile against registry contents, and (b) per-action attestation published at kernel level with measured publication latencies in the sub-microsecond-to-microsecond range. The document defines a traceability record, states what a verifier can and cannot conclude from a set of such records, and identifies the points at
which existing agent-protocol work - identity, authorisation, and transport - needs a common traceability layer. It defines no wire protocol of its own; it states the requirements a traceability mechanism must satisfy so that formats defined elsewhere can be evaluated against them.
